glance.does: Cart totals now count quantity, and orders over $100 get 10% off.
glance.forUser: Buying two of something costs twice as much; big orders cost less.
glance.lookAt: The discount hard-codes 100 and 0.9 instead of using the new constants.

steps.title: Count quantity
steps.summary: The total multiplies each price by its quantity.

steps.title: Discount big orders
steps.summary: Totals over $100 take 10% off, and the numbers get their own file.
steps.why: Applied after summing so rounding matches the receipt.

evidence.quote: Applied after summing so rounding matches the receipt.

steps.title: Clean up
steps.summary: Old notes removed, one file renamed, a logo added.

intent.summary: Orders over $100 get 10% off, and the cart total now multiplies price by quantity instead of ignoring it.

beforeAfter.before: Two of an item counted once.

slices.title: Cleanup
slices.summary: Removed and renamed files, new logo.

evidence.quote: a per-item discount would round differently

decisions.why: Probably so other modules can share them.

visuals.title: How the total is computed
visuals.caption: The discount is a new last step.
visuals.before:
flowchart LR
  A[Items] --> B[Sum prices] --> C[Total]
visuals.after:
flowchart LR
  A[Items] --> B[Sum price x qty] --> D{Over 100?}
  D -- yes --> E[x 0.9] --> C[Total]
  D -- no --> C

mismatches.claim: The discount uses the shared constants.
mismatches.observed: cart.ts hard-codes 100 and 0.9; DISCOUNT and THRESHOLD are unused.

risks.title: Constants drift from the code
risks.scenario: Someone changes DISCOUNT to 0.85; carts still take 10% off.

risks.title: Exactly $100 gets no discount
risks.scenario: A $100.00 cart pays full price because the check is > not >=.

options.change: Import DISCOUNT and THRESHOLD in cart.ts

options.tradeoff: Changes who gets the discount; check with the business rule.
